about.title: Los Banos Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a crash changes everything, and the last thing anyone should have to manage during that time is a legal fight. In Los Banos, where traffic moves through corridors like Rt 152, E and W Pacheco Boulevard, and Rt 165, families sometimes find themselves facing a wrongful death claim after a collision took someone they loved. California law lets certain surviving family members — usually a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, then other dependents or heirs — pursue compensation for funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a person provided. This is a civil claim, separate from any criminal proceedings that might follow the same incident. LawProactive doesn't practice law or represent your family directly. Instead, we connect grieving families in Los Banos with an independent personal injury attorney, free of charge, so you can get informed guidance about your options while you focus on your family.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Move Forward

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse, domestic partner, and children first, then other dependents or heirs if none exist. An attorney can help clarify who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and claims against a government entity can require notice much sooner. Waiting too long can permanently close the door on recovery.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek compensation for funeral costs and lost financial support, but also for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a person gave their family. An attorney can help you understand the full scope of what may be recoverable.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Los Banos?
items.answer: California generally gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government agency, like a public road authority in Merced County, may be involved, the deadline to give notice can be much shorter. Speaking with an attorney early helps make sure your family doesn't lose the ability to pursue a claim.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring this claim?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children. If there is no spouse or children, other dependents or heirs may have standing to file. An attorney can review your family's specific situation to determine who qualifies.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to any criminal charges against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case, even if both arise from the same crash on a road like Rt 152 or Rt 165. Criminal charges focus on punishment, while a civil claim focuses on compensating the family for their losses. The outcome of one does not determine the outcome of the other.
